address.en: to deal with or try to solve a problem

advocate for.en: a person who publicly supports an idea or cause

analogous to.en: similar to something in some way, so the two can be compared

analyzing.en: examining something carefully to understand it

annotate.en: to add notes or comments to a text or picture

anticipated.en: expected or predicted that something would happen

assembled.en: gathered together or put the parts of something together

atypical.en: not usual or typical; different from what is normal

beneficiary of.en: a person or thing that receives help or an advantage from something

bolster.en: to support or strengthen something, such as a claim

borrowed from.en: taken from another source and used

buttress.en: to support or strengthen an argument or claim

challenged.en: questioned whether something is true or right

champion of.en: a person who strongly supports and fights for a cause

choosing.en: picking one thing from several possibilities

circumvent.en: to find a way around a problem or rule

comparable to.en: similar enough in size, amount, or quality to be compared

conceptualize.en: to form an idea of something in your mind

critic of.en: a person who disapproves of or criticizes something

defender of.en: a person who protects or argues in support of something

define.en: to explain the exact meaning of something

denied.en: said that something is not true; refused to accept

deny.en: to say that something is not true

denying.en: saying that something is not true

derived from.en: coming from or developed from a source

describe.en: to say what something is like

detecting.en: noticing or discovering something that is hard to see

devised.en: planned or invented a new method or system

disengage.en: to separate from or stop being involved in something

dismiss.en: to decide something is not important or worth considering

distraction for.en: something that takes attention away (used incorrectly here with "for")

distraction from.en: something that takes your attention away from something else

document.en: to record information in writing, photos, etc.

equivalent to.en: equal in value, amount, or meaning

estimated.en: guessed an amount or value based on information

exceptional.en: very unusual; much better or different than normal

forecast.en: to predict what will happen in the future

ignore.en: to pay no attention to something

illustrate.en: to explain or show something with examples or pictures

illustrated.en: explained with examples or drew pictures for

imitate.en: to copy the way someone or something does things

imitated.en: copied the way someone or something does things

independent of.en: not controlled by or connected to something

inferior to.en: not as good as something else

inspecting.en: looking at something closely to check it

inventing.en: creating something that did not exist before

lucrative.en: producing a lot of money; profitable

minimized.en: made something as small as possible, or treated it as unimportant

neglect.en: to fail to give enough care or attention to something

obtained from.en: gotten or acquired from a source

overcome.en: to succeed in dealing with a problem or difficulty

postponing.en: delaying something until a later time

predicted.en: said what would happen in the future

projected.en: estimated what a future amount or result will be

proponent of.en: a person who supports an idea or plan

rare.en: not happening or found very often

reciprocate.en: to do or feel the same thing in return

reinforce.en: to make an idea, claim, or structure stronger

replaced.en: put something new in the place of something else

replicate.en: to copy or repeat something exactly, such as an experiment

resolve.en: to find a solution to a problem

restored.en: brought back to an earlier good condition

reviewing.en: looking at or studying something again

scrutinizing.en: examining something very carefully and in detail

separate from.en: not joined or connected to something

substantiate.en: to provide evidence to prove that something is true

supplement to.en: something added to complete or improve something

support.en: to help show that something is true; to back an idea

supporter of.en: a person who agrees with and helps an idea or group

surmount.en: to deal successfully with a difficulty

surpassed by.en: done better than or exceeded by

tedious.en: boring because it is long or repetitive

unusual.en: different from what is normal or expected

validated.en: proved that something is true or correct

withdraw.en: to take back or remove; to pull out of something

worsen.en: to become or make something worse
